Banana___Healthy.safety_precautions: Follow standard farm hygiene and sanitation practices. Wear protective gloves during field labor.
Banana___Healthy.dosage_guidelines: Apply balanced organic compost and recommended NPK split doses per local agricultural recommendations.
Banana___Healthy.organic_alternatives: Bio-fertilizers (Azospirillum, Phosphobacteria), Panchagavya, farmyard manure, mulching with crop residue.
Banana___Healthy.disclaimer: No chemical pesticide treatment needed for healthy crop. Maintain regular field monitoring and sanitation.
Banana___Healthy.reference_sources: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), TNAU Agritech Portal

Banana___Panama_Disease.safety_precautions: Avoid soil contamination. Wear gloves, boots, and mask during soil drenching. Prevent runoff into irrigation channels.
Banana___Panama_Disease.dosage_guidelines: Soil drenching around pseudostem base with Carbendazim 0.2% (2g/L water) or Trichoderma viride bio-agent (10g/plant) mixed with FYM.
Banana___Panama_Disease.organic_alternatives: Soil application of Trichoderma viride, Pseudomonas fluorescens, crop rotation with non-host crops, planting resistant cultivars (Grand Naine / Cavendish).
Banana___Panama_Disease.disclaimer: Fungal pathogen persists in soil. Severely infected pseudostems should be uprooted, limed, and safely destroyed outside the farm.
Banana___Panama_Disease.reference_sources: FAO Crop Protection Guidelines, ICAR-NRCB Extension Bulletins

Banana___Yellow_Black_Sigatoka.active_ingredient: Propiconazole 25% EC / Mancozeb 75% WP / Mineral Oil emulsion
Banana___Yellow_Black_Sigatoka.safety_precautions: Wear personal protective equipment (goggles, mask, gloves). Do not spray during windy conditions or high sun. Observe 14-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI).
Banana___Yellow_Black_Sigatoka.dosage_guidelines: Spray Propiconazole at 1 ml/L or Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L with mineral oil (10 ml/L) as sticker at early streak appearance.
Banana___Yellow_Black_Sigatoka.organic_alternatives: De-leafing of affected lower leaves, canopy ventilation, spraying Neem oil 1% (10 ml/L), application of Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L).
Banana___Yellow_Black_Sigatoka.disclaimer: Rotate chemical fungicide classes to avoid fungicide resistance. Follow local product label instructions.
Banana___Yellow_Black_Sigatoka.reference_sources: TNAU Agritech Portal - Banana Plant Protection, ICAR-NRCB

Bell_Pepper___Bacterial_Spot.safety_precautions: Avoid inhalation of copper spray drift. Wear full protective suit, safety glasses, and gloves. Do not contaminate water bodies.
Bell_Pepper___Bacterial_Spot.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride at 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline (or Agrimycin) at 0.1 g/L at first sign of spots.
Bell_Pepper___Bacterial_Spot.organic_alternatives: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg seed), spraying copper hydroxide (2g/L), overhead irrigation avoidance, disease-free seed selection.
Bell_Pepper___Bacterial_Spot.disclaimer: Bacterial pathogens spread rapidly via splashing rain and overhead watering. Use drip irrigation where possible.
Bell_Pepper___Bacterial_Spot.reference_sources: ICAR Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), TNAU Agritech Portal

Bell_Pepper___Healthy.safety_precautions: Maintain field sanitation and wear protective gloves during pruning and harvesting.
Bell_Pepper___Healthy.dosage_guidelines: Maintain balanced calcium and boron fertigation to prevent blossom end rot alongside normal NPK management.
Bell_Pepper___Healthy.organic_alternatives: Neem cake application in soil, installing yellow sticky traps (10/acre) for preventive insect monitoring.
Bell_Pepper___Healthy.disclaimer: Plant is healthy. Continue preventive field hygiene and weed management.

Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.safety_precautions: Wear mask, goggles, and chemical-resistant gloves during chemical mixing and application. Avoid spraying before rain.
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L) mixed with Streptocycline (0.1g/L). Repeat after 12-15 days if necessary.
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.organic_alternatives: Seed delinting and delinted seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg seed), field destruction of infected crop debris, crop rotation.
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.disclaimer: Use certified disease-free seeds and avoid field entry when foliage is wet.

Cotton___Curl_Virus.safety_precautions: Strictly observe safety precautions when handling systemic insecticides. Wear gloves and protective mask. Observe 21-day PHI.
Cotton___Curl_Virus.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L or Diafenthiuron at 1g/L to control whitefly vector population below economic threshold level (ETL).
Cotton___Curl_Virus.organic_alternatives: Yellow sticky traps (20/acre), spraying Neem oil 1500 ppm (5 ml/L), planting castor as border trap crop, growing resistant cotton hybrids.
Cotton___Curl_Virus.disclaimer: Viral diseases cannot be cured with chemical sprays after infection; vector control and rogueing infected plants are vital.
Cotton___Curl_Virus.reference_sources: ICAR-CICR Nagpur, State Agricultural University Extension

Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.safety_precautions: Wear rubber boots and gloves during soil treatment. Ensure chemical disposal follows local environmental guidelines.
Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.dosage_guidelines: Soil drenching near root zone with Carbendazim 0.1% (1g/L water) or soil enrichment with Trichoderma viride (2.5 kg/acre in FYM).
Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.organic_alternatives: Soil solarization during summer, application of Trichoderma viride enriched FYM, crop rotation with non-host crops like sorghum or maize.
Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.disclaimer: Avoid planting susceptible cultivars in field plots with a history of Fusarium wilt.
Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.reference_sources: ICAR-CICR Cotton Advisory, TNAU Agritech Portal

Cotton___Healthy.safety_precautions: Follow safe farm practices. Handle fertilizers with clean gloves.
Cotton___Healthy.dosage_guidelines: Follow recommended NPK fertilizer schedule and maintain field drainage.
Cotton___Healthy.organic_alternatives: Pheromone traps for bollworm monitoring, light traps, neem cake soil amendment.
Cotton___Healthy.disclaimer: Crop foliage shows healthy growth. Maintain IPM monitoring.

Eggplant___Healthy.safety_precautions: Practice standard crop hygiene and wear gloves during harvesting.
Eggplant___Healthy.dosage_guidelines: Apply balanced micronutrient foliar spray (zinc/boron) if required per soil test.
Eggplant___Healthy.organic_alternatives: Pheromone traps for fruit borer monitoring, yellow/blue sticky traps, neem oil preventive spray.
Eggplant___Healthy.disclaimer: No disease symptoms detected. Maintain field hygiene.

Eggplant___Insect_Pest.disease: Insect Pest Damage (Fruit & Shoot Borer / Epilachna Beetle)
Eggplant___Insect_Pest.active_ingredient: Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG / Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC / Neem formulation
Eggplant___Insect_Pest.safety_precautions: Wear protective gear (mask, gloves, long sleeves). Do not harvest fruits within 5-7 days of chemical spray (observe PHI).
Eggplant___Insect_Pest.dosage_guidelines: Spray Emamectin Benzoate at 0.4 g/L or Chlorantraniliprole at 0.3 ml/L of water at shoot wilt or early fruit damage.
Eggplant___Insect_Pest.organic_alternatives: Clip affected shoot tips promptly, install Lucinode pheromone traps (12/acre), spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2g/L or Neem oil (5ml/L).
Eggplant___Insect_Pest.disclaimer: Prompt clipping of infested shoots is essential to reduce borer populations.
Eggplant___Insect_Pest.reference_sources: ICAR-IIHR Vegetable Protection Manual, TNAU Agritech

Eggplant___Leaf_Spot.safety_precautions: Wear mask and gloves during preparation and application. Avoid spraying before rain or during strong wind.
Eggplant___Leaf_Spot.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L or Copper Oxychloride at 2.5 g/L at 10-14 day intervals.
Eggplant___Leaf_Spot.organic_alternatives: Destroy infected lower leaves, spray Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L), apply Panchagavya 3% as foliar boost.
Eggplant___Leaf_Spot.disclaimer: Avoid dense spacing to improve airflow through crop canopy.

Eggplant___Mosaic_Virus.active_ingredient: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL / Thiamethoxam 25% WG (for aphid vector control)
Eggplant___Mosaic_Virus.safety_precautions: Wear protective equipment during vector spray. Keep children and animals away from spray zone.
Eggplant___Mosaic_Virus.dosage_guidelines: Spray Thiamethoxam at 0.3 g/L or Imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L to manage aphid vectors.
Eggplant___Mosaic_Virus.organic_alternatives: Rogue out infected plants immediately, place yellow sticky traps, spray Neem oil 1500 ppm (5 ml/L), maintain weed-free borders.
Eggplant___Mosaic_Virus.disclaimer: Plant viruses cannot be cured once established. Vector suppression and rogueing infected plants prevent field spread.

Eggplant___Small_Leaf.safety_precautions: Wear protective clothing and respiratory mask. Observe strict PHI before harvesting brinjal fruits.
Eggplant___Small_Leaf.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Dimethoate at 1.7 ml/L or Imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L to control leafhopper vectors.
Eggplant___Small_Leaf.organic_alternatives: Uproot and burn little-leaf infected plants, spray Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%), use barrier crops like maize.
Eggplant___Small_Leaf.disclaimer: Prompt destruction of early infected plants is critical as phytoplasma spreads via leafhoppers.
Eggplant___Small_Leaf.reference_sources: TNAU Agritech Portal - Little Leaf of Brinjal

Eggplant___White_Mold.safety_precautions: Wear chemical resistant gloves, goggles, and mask. Avoid skin contact and wash thoroughly post application.
Eggplant___White_Mold.dosage_guidelines: Spray Carbendazim at 1 g/L or Tebuconazole blend at 0.7 g/L at disease onset around stem base and leaves.
Eggplant___White_Mold.organic_alternatives: Soil treatment with Trichoderma harzianum, crop rotation with non-susceptible crops (cereals/grasses), avoiding waterlogging.
Eggplant___White_Mold.disclaimer: Sclerotia fungal bodies survive long in soil. Improve field drainage and crop spacing.

Eggplant___Wilt.safety_precautions: Wear rubber boots and gloves during soil drenching. Prevent chemical contamination of natural water streams.
Eggplant___Wilt.dosage_guidelines: Drench soil around plants with Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1g/L) or apply Trichoderma viride (10g/L).
Eggplant___Wilt.organic_alternatives: Grafting on resistant wild brinjal rootstock (Solanum torvum), soil solarization, applying Pseudomonas fluorescens in soil.
Eggplant___Wilt.disclaimer: Severely wilted plants will not recover; uproot and destroy them safely.

Potato___Early_Blight.safety_precautions: Wear protective gear (goggles, mask, gloves). Do not spray within 7 days of tuber harvest.
Potato___Early_Blight.dosage_guidelines: Spray Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil at 2 g/L at first appearance of target-like brown spots on foliage.
Potato___Early_Blight.organic_alternatives: Foliar spray of Trichoderma viride (10g/L), Neem oil 1% spray, removing infected lower leaves, balanced potash fertilization.
Potato___Early_Blight.disclaimer: Maintain adequate plant nutrition; nitrogen and potassium deficiency increases susceptibility.

Potato___Healthy.safety_precautions: Practice standard agricultural safety during earthing up and irrigation.
Potato___Healthy.dosage_guidelines: Apply adequate potassium and nitrogen split doses alongside proper earthing up to prevent greening of tubers.
Potato___Healthy.organic_alternatives: Well-rotted farmyard manure, bio-fertilizer soil application, crop rotation with legumes.
Potato___Healthy.disclaimer: Potato crop shows healthy foliage. Continue preventive monitoring.

Potato___Late_Blight.safety_precautions: Late blight spreads rapidly. Wear full protective suit, mask, and goggles. Observe 14-day Pre-Harvest Interval.
Potato___Late_Blight.dosage_guidelines: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil blend at 2 g/L immediately when humid/cloudy weather favours blight.
Potato___Late_Blight.organic_alternatives: Preventive spray of Copper Hydroxide (2g/L), destroying infected vines (haulm cutting) before harvest, resistant varieties (Kufri Girdhari).
Potato___Late_Blight.disclaimer: Late blight can destroy fields in days under humid conditions. Apply systemic fungicides promptly upon early symptoms.

Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.safety_precautions: Wear mask and gloves during chemical mixing. Drain excess water from field during severe blight outbreak.
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Copper Oxychloride at 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline at 0.15 g/L. Drain field water temporarily.
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.organic_alternatives: Foliar spray of fresh cow dung extract (20%), spraying Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L), avoiding excess nitrogenous fertilizer.
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.disclaimer: Reduce nitrogen application during outbreak. Avoid field irrigation transfer from infected to healthy plots.

Rice___Brown_Spot.safety_precautions: Wear gloves and face mask during application. Observe 15-day PHI.
Rice___Brown_Spot.dosage_guidelines: Spray Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L or Propiconazole at 1 ml/L. Apply soil potassium and zinc sulphate if nutrient deficient.
Rice___Brown_Spot.organic_alternatives: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride (10g/kg seed), balanced soil nutrient management (soil test based NPK + Zn).
Rice___Brown_Spot.disclaimer: Brown spot is heavily associated with nutrient-deficient or poor soils. Correct soil potassium and zinc levels.

Rice___Healthy.safety_precautions: Follow standard safety practices during fertilizer top-dressing.
Rice___Healthy.dosage_guidelines: Maintain alternate wetting and drying (AWD) water management and recommended split nitrogen doses.
Rice___Healthy.organic_alternatives: Azolla bio-fertilizer incorporation, green manuring with Sesbania, neem coated urea.
Rice___Healthy.disclaimer: Paddy crop foliage is clean and healthy. Maintain AWD water practices.

Rice___Leaf_Blast.safety_precautions: Wear mask, goggles, and gloves. Do not contaminate fish ponds or nearby waterways. Observe 21-day PHI.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Tricyclazole at 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane at 1.5 ml/L at spindle-shaped leaf spot stage or boot leaf stage.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.organic_alternatives: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg seed), foliar spray of Pseudomonas (10g/L), avoiding excessive evening nitrogen.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.disclaimer: Blast fungal spores proliferate in high humidity and cool night temperatures.

Rice___Leaf_Scald.safety_precautions: Wear protective gloves and dust mask. Follow local pesticide disposal guidelines.
Rice___Leaf_Scald.dosage_guidelines: Spray Carbendazim at 1 g/L or Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L at early leaf band scalding symptoms.
Rice___Leaf_Scald.organic_alternatives: Use disease-free seed, treat seeds with Trichoderma (10g/kg), avoid dense nursery sowing.
Rice___Leaf_Scald.disclaimer: Ensure proper spacing and weed removal in field borders.

Rice___Sheath_Blight.safety_precautions: Direct spray towards the lower stem and sheath zone. Wear chemical-resistant boots, gloves, and mask.
Rice___Sheath_Blight.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Validamycin at 2 ml/L or Hexaconazole at 2 ml/L targeting the lower sheath canopy level.
Rice___Sheath_Blight.organic_alternatives: Soil application of Trichoderma viride, spraying Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L), clearing weed hosts from bunds.
Rice___Sheath_Blight.disclaimer: Fungus survives in soil and irrigation water; direct chemical spray to lower sheath region.

Tomato___Bacterial_Spot.safety_precautions: Wear goggles, face mask, and gloves. Do not apply during high heat or before rain.
Tomato___Bacterial_Spot.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1g/L) at 10-day intervals.
Tomato___Bacterial_Spot.organic_alternatives: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg), copper hydroxide spray (2g/L), avoiding overhead sprinkler irrigation.
Tomato___Bacterial_Spot.disclaimer: Bacterial spot spreads rapidly through water droplets. Use drip irrigation and prune lower foliage.
Tomato___Bacterial_Spot.reference_sources: ICAR-IIHR Tomato Disease Manual, TNAU Agritech

Tomato___Early_Blight.safety_precautions: Wear personal protective equipment (mask, gloves). Observe 7-day PHI before fruit picking.
Tomato___Early_Blight.dosage_guidelines: Spray Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L or Azoxystrobin at 1 ml/L at first sight of concentric target spots on foliage.
Tomato___Early_Blight.organic_alternatives: Mulching soil to prevent spore splash, pruning bottom 30cm foliage, spraying Trichoderma viride (10g/L) or Neem oil 1%.
Tomato___Early_Blight.disclaimer: Staking tomatoes and mulching significantly reduces early blight leaf infection from soil spores.

Tomato___Healthy.dosage_guidelines: Maintain regular fertigation with calcium nitrate to prevent blossom end rot.
Tomato___Healthy.organic_alternatives: Neem oil preventive spray (3ml/L), yellow sticky traps for whiteflies, bio-fertilizer soil drench.
Tomato___Healthy.disclaimer: Plant foliage is healthy. Ensure adequate staking and irrigation consistency.

Tomato___Late_Blight.safety_precautions: High risk disease. Wear full protective suit, goggles, and respiratory mask. Observe 14-day PHI.
Tomato___Late_Blight.dosage_guidelines: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil blend at 2 g/L upon humid/cool weather alert.
Tomato___Late_Blight.organic_alternatives: Spray Copper Hydroxide (2g/L), remove and destroy blighted foliage immediately, ensure wide plant spacing.
Tomato___Late_Blight.disclaimer: Cool, wet weather triggers rapid late blight outbreak. Act immediately upon symptom observation.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.safety_precautions: Wear mask and protective clothing. Ensure adequate greenhouse/field ventilation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Difenoconazole at 0.5 ml/L or Chlorothalonil at 2 g/L targeting leaf undersides.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.organic_alternatives: Improve greenhouse airflow and lower humidity below 85%, spray bio-agent Trichoderma harzianum (10g/L).
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.disclaimer: Leaf mold thrives in humid, enclosed conditions. Prune lower leaves to enhance air circulation.

Tomato___Mosaic_Virus.active_ingredient: Trisodium Phosphate (for tool sterilization) / Imidacloprid (for vector control)
Tomato___Mosaic_Virus.safety_precautions: Wash hands with soap/milk before handling tomato plants. Disinfect pruners and stakes.
Tomato___Mosaic_Virus.dosage_guidelines: Dip tools in 10% Trisodium Phosphate or skimmed milk solution. Spray Imidacloprid (0.5ml/L) for sap-sucking insect control.
Tomato___Mosaic_Virus.organic_alternatives: Rogue out infected mosaic plants, spray skimmed milk (200ml/L water) as mechanical barrier, use resistant seed varieties.
Tomato___Mosaic_Virus.disclaimer: ToMV spreads mechanically via workers' hands and tools. Strictly observe field hygiene.

Tomato___Septoria_Leaf_Spot.safety_precautions: Wear mask, goggles, and gloves. Do not apply when plants are wet.
Tomato___Septoria_Leaf_Spot.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Mancozeb at 2.5 g/L or Copper Oxychloride at 2.5 g/L starting at lower leaf spot detection.
Tomato___Septoria_Leaf_Spot.organic_alternatives: Remove infected lower foliage, apply straw mulch to prevent soil rain splash, spray Neem oil 1%.
Tomato___Septoria_Leaf_Spot.disclaimer: Septoria fungus overwinters in plant debris. Rotate tomato crop with non-solanaceous crops.
Tomato___Septoria_Leaf_Spot.reference_sources: TNAU Agritech Portal - Tomato Septoria Spot

Tomato___Spider_Mites.active_ingredient: Abamectin 1.9% EC / Spiromesifen 22.9% SC / Wettable Sulphur
Tomato___Spider_Mites.safety_precautions: Wear full protective clothing and face mask. Avoid spraying beneficial insects like bees during bloom.
Tomato___Spider_Mites.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Spiromesifen at 1 ml/L or Abamectin at 0.5 ml/L targeting leaf undersides where mites colonize.
Tomato___Spider_Mites.organic_alternatives: Spray Wettable Sulphur at 3 g/L or Neem oil 1500 ppm (5 ml/L), spray high-pressure water jets on leaf undersides, release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus).
Tomato___Spider_Mites.disclaimer: Hot and dry weather causes rapid mite multiplication. Direct sprays to undersides of leaves.

Tomato___Target_Spot.safety_precautions: Wear gloves and protective mask during mixing and spraying.
Tomato___Target_Spot.dosage_guidelines: Foliar spray Chlorothalonil at 2 g/L or Azoxystrobin at 1 ml/L at onset of brown target lesions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.organic_alternatives: Field sanitation, crop canopy pruning, foliar spray of Trichoderma viride (10g/L).
Tomato___Target_Spot.disclaimer: Ensure good drainage and canopy ventilation to manage humidity.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.safety_precautions: Wear chemical-resistant gloves, coveralls, and face mask. Observe 14-day PHI.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.dosage_guidelines: Spray Cyantraniliprole at 1.8 ml/L or Imidacloprid at 0.5 ml/L to suppress Bemisia tabaci whitefly vectors.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_alternatives: Install yellow sticky traps (25/acre), erect 50-mesh insect net around nursery/farm, spray Neem oil 1500 ppm (5ml/L), plant resistant varieties.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.disclaimer: TYLCV causes severe stunt and yield loss. Early vector suppression and physical screening are crucial.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.reference_sources: ICAR-IIHR Whitefly & TYLCV Extension Bulletin, TNAU Agritech
